summary.text: A 35-year-old woman, gravida 4 para 3 with three previous cesarean deliveries, presented asymptomatic at 6 weeks and 5 days of gestation. Ultrasound showed a gestational sac implanted at the site of the previous cesarean scar, consistent with cesarean scar pregnancy. She was counseled, offered termination, expressed a desire to preserve fertility, opted against termination and was placed under close follow-up.

An anomaly scan at 18 weeks was normal, but ultrasound findings were consistent with total placenta previa and showed features suggestive of placenta percreta, including bridging vessels, multiple placental lakes and myometrial thinning; the abstract states percreta was diagnosed at 18 weeks. Despite repeated counseling about the risks she chose to continue the pregnancy.

At 29 weeks she had a mild vaginal bleeding episode with stable vital signs and was admitted; ultrasound confirmed persistent placenta percreta. She received magnesium sulfate and two doses of betamethasone, the bleeding resolved after 72 hr and she was discharged with monitoring instructions. At 32 weeks and 1 day she was readmitted with recurrent bleeding, remained hemodynamically stable and received a rescue dose of betamethasone.

A cesarean delivery through a fundal incision delivered a breech female infant of 1690 grams with an Apgar score of 8–9, and a hysterectomy was performed because of severe lower uterine segment adhesions; the placenta was kept in situ and removed intact with the uterus, ovaries preserved, and sent to pathology. Blood loss was about 2,000 ml with one unit transfused. Recovery was uneventful, with discharge on postoperative day 3; fertility was permanently lost.
